You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get “details about rich visitors,” we need a definition of **rich** (usually based on `visit.Total_spent`, either per visit or total across all visits). Here are common options—pick one that matches what you mean.

### 1) Visitors with the highest **total spending** (overall)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

### 2) “Rich” = total spending above a threshold (e.g., > 1000)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
HAVING SUM(vi.Total_spent) > 1000
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

### 3) “Rich” = biggest **single-visit** spenders
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  MAX(vi.Total_spent) AS max_single_visit_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY max_single_visit_spent DESC;
```

Which definition do you want (total spent vs single-visit), and do you want a **top N** (e.g., top 10) or a **minimum spending threshold**?
I want details on who bought the most tickets.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want **all ties** (everyone who bought the same maximum number of tickets):

```sql
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT visitor_ID, SUM(Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
  FROM visit
  GROUP BY visitor_ID
),
mx AS (
  SELECT MAX(total_tickets) AS max_tickets FROM totals
)
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  t.total_tickets
FROM totals t
JOIN mx ON t.total_tickets = mx.max_tickets
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = t.visitor_ID;
```
also include the visitor's name in the details

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also, make sure the ticket purchase was done in a single transaction.

Use the **maximum `Num_of_Ticket` in a single row of `visit`** (one transaction), then return the visitor details for that transaction:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_in_single_transaction,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket) FROM visit);
```

If multiple transactions tie for the max, this returns all of them. If you want just one, add `LIMIT 1` at the end.
oh, also I want to include the visitor's age too

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_in_single_transaction,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
WHERE vi.Num_of_Ticket = (SELECT MAX(Num_of_Ticket) FROM visit);
```
